title: [AUG-207] Research: stop updates from moving August to a new install folder and leaving the user's data behind (Windows)
why_we_need_this: On 2026-11-09 (22:35 UTC) the silent auto-update to 0.2.0 (`--updated /S --force-run`) installed August into the default `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Programs\August` instead of the existing install `D:\claude\August\installed`. Every update from 0.0.35 to 0.1.4 had landed on D:. On Windows the data dir is `<install dir>\data` (@electron/src/main.ts:104), so the new copy started with an empty `data`. To the user this looked like the update "wiped" everything: 10 sessions, preferences and the `.env` holding GROQ_API_KEY seemed gone. 0.2.1 arrived 6 minutes later and was blamed. The old data survived untouched in `D:\claude\August\installed\data`. Afterwards `HKCU\Software\8ed30dcd-7880-51a9-bc47-ea538a6afaa3\InstallLocation` held the C: path. Recovery was a manual `/S /D=D:\claude\August\installed` reinstall. AUG-158 only protects `data` inside the same install folder, so it cannot catch this. Any user who installed to a custom folder can hit the same silent "data loss". The cause of the registry change is not proven yet.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Root cause found from evidence (electron-builder NSIS multiUser/installSection sources for the version in use, registry behaviour, tests in a throwaway Windows profile or VM): which steps make `InstallLocation` (HKCU `Software\{appGuid}`) stop pointing at a custom folder, e.g. a second install or uninstall into the default folder, an MSI target install (the `msi` target in @electron/electron-builder.yml shares the app GUID), or an uninstall that deletes the key. Each scenario is reproduced or ruled out, with steps written down.
- [ ] Analysis of where data should live: compare keeping `<install dir>\data` (current, D13/0.0.13 decision) with moving to a path that does not depend on the install folder (`%APPDATA%\August\data` or a pointer file in userData, like `model-dir` / `llm-location.json`). Cover migration, the AUG-158 installer logic, the 8.3 / non-ASCII path handling and the macOS path (must stay unchanged).
- [ ] At least 3 prevention options with pros and cons, for example: the installer refuses or warns when `--updated` targets a folder different from the running app's folder; the app keeps a data-dir pointer in `%APPDATA%\August` and on startup with an empty `data` finds the previous data dir and offers a one-click move; the updater passes `/D=<current install dir>` to the installer; drop or isolate the MSI target.
- [ ] A recommended option, and a list of the impl tasks it needs (scope, affected files, risks for both platforms). Impl tasks are proposed in the result, not created without user approval.
- [ ] Findings are recorded in the desktop-shell project-context route (the update/data-preservation section).
important_constraints:
- Research only: no changes to installer.nsh, main.ts, config.ts or electron-builder.yml in this task.
- Never run installers or uninstallers against the user's real install (`D:\claude\August\installed`) or touch its `data`. Use a separate Windows user profile, VM or sandbox with a test appId/productName.
- macOS keeps `~/Library/Application Support/August/data`; any proposal must stay a no-op on darwin (project CLAUDE.md cross-platform rules).
- Evidence for the incident: `%APPDATA%\August\logs\main.log` (lines with AUGUST_DATA_DIR and [updater], 2026-11-09 22:34–22:42 UTC), the registry keys above, @electron/build/installer.nsh, @electron/electron-builder.yml (nsis + msi targets).
- Related: AUG-158 (NSIS update data preservation).

## Research result (2026-11-16)
- **Root cause:** the 0.0.45 → 0.1.4 silent update (2026-11-05 13:50 UTC) was cut by a BSOD (bugcheck 0x139, reboot 14:00:59 UTC) after the old uninstaller had deleted HKCU `Software\{appGuid}` and the Uninstall key and before the installer wrote them back. 0.1.4 kept working from D: with no registry trace; the 0.2.0 update on 11-09 found no InstallLocation and used `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\August`. 0.2.1 was not the cause.
- **Ruled out for this incident:** MSI install, manual uninstall, second manual install, dev/test installer runs. Possible in general: an interactive reinstall into another folder strands data the same way.
- **No live reproduction** (user decision 2026-11-16: no sandbox, VM or second profile available); verdicts come from electron-builder 26.15.3 NSIS templates, main.log, file timestamps and the System event log.
- **Recommendation:** A + B. A: updater passes `/D=<folder of the running exe>` (`autoUpdater.installDirectory`, win32 only). B: data-dir pointer `%APPDATA%\August\data-location.json` so data no longer follows the install folder. Not recommended: fixed `%APPDATA%\August\data` (cross-volume move, ignores the user's drive choice); dropping MSI (not involved).
- **Proposed impl tasks (not created):** 1) updater pins the install folder (@electron/src/updater.ts); 2) sticky data dir (@electron/src/main.ts win32 branch + pure module with tests, pointer cleanup in @electron/build/installer.nsh); 3) optional installer hardening (rewrite InstallLocation right after the old uninstaller, warn on folder change).
- **Full write-up:** @project-context/desktop-shell/README.md, section "Install folder drift and data left behind (AUG-207)".
- **Leftover on this PC:** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\August\data` from the 15-minute stray run on 11-09; not touched.
